newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Aukland rises after black empowerment buy.
newsitem.headline: Aukland rises after black empowerment buy.

text.p: Shares in South African healthcare firm Aukland Investments rose over six percent on news that a black empowerment group had bought a stake in the firm, and after some initial profit taking after the deal.

Dealers said that the market welcomed news on Wednesday that Pamodzi Investment Holdings Ltd had bought a 26 percent stake in Aukland for 46 million rand. Pamodzi also said that it was planning eight new investments over the next two years.
By 0959 GMT on Thursday Aukland shares added 30 cents to 500 cents, nearing its 1997 high of 550 cents in volume of 106,900 shares.

"(The rise) must be on the deal. There's been no other news about Aukland. It's quite a thinly traded share," a dealer said, adding that the shares were also gaining ground after initially sagging 50 cents on Wednesday to close at 470 cents.
"It's the classic case of buy on rumour, sell on fact. They had a cautionary out so people bought and then sold when it was confirmed," the dealer said.
Pamodzi acquired its stake in Aukland by taking up shares renounced by the controlling shareholders in a 71 million rand rights issue.

Established last year, Pamodzi which means "we are one" in Swahili, aims to invest in industries with good growth prospects, experienced management, strong prospects for cash generation and good returns.

Aukland's assets consist of HospiPlan, managing 14 private hospitals, Othorsurge, a distributor of medical equipment, Unisurge, a surgical instrument distributor and Disamed, a pharmaceutical wholesaler.
